requirement_paraphrase: Demonstrate that the system to be deployed is valid and reliable; document limits on generalisability beyond the conditions under which it was developed.

Digital investment managers must document the model's decision logic so outputs are explainable, traceable and repeatable, check data and assumptions stay relevant, and run sufficient, regular testing to show the model meets these principles. For complex models the FSRA may require a third-party audit of performance claims.
Operators must review in advance whether their AI is high-impact and may ask the Minister to confirm.

SFDA is to be informed via GHAD of significant changes within 10 days; the manufacturer shall have QMS procedures for change control, and all changes shall be evaluated, verified and validated under those procedures.
Evaluate regularly for safety risks; demonstrate that the system to be deployed is safe, residual risk does not exceed tolerance, and it can fail safely, including beyond its knowledge limits.
Recommends systematic cybersecurity code review, testing and formal approval of all AI-generated code before use in development, integration or production.

Litmus is described as a Singapore government service for testing LLM apps of agencies with 1,600 prompts across security, specialised advice, undesirable and political content; default threshold 95 percent safe responses, adjustable; even a single failure in high-stakes hard-gate cases requires investigation.
Establish minimum thresholds for performance or assurance criteria and review them as part of deployment approval (go/no-go) policies, procedures and processes.
The controller must periodically review the outcomes of the impact assessment where the level of risk changes.
Technical report giving an overview of existing methods for assessing the robustness of neural networks, particularly when conditions change; published 10 Mar 2021, 31 pages.

Before processing that uses modern technologies and poses a high risk to privacy and confidentiality, the controller must assess the impact of the planned processing. Mandatory cases include systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects by automated processing (including profiling) with legal or serious effects, and large-scale processing of sensitive data. Minimum content: description and purpose, necessity and suitability, privacy risk assessment, and mitigation measures.

clause_or_page: Outcome 7.1 / Process 7.1.1, p.71 (technical testing, traditional AI)
requirement_paraphrase: System owner selects fairness metrics for sensitive features and measures disparity of error rates across groups.

Draft provides voluntary preliminary best practices for automated benchmark evaluations of language models and AI agent systems, in three stages: define objectives, implement/run, analyse/report; scoped to existing benchmarks, not creating new ones.

Content red teaming probes the app dynamically for blind spots, multi-turn failures and subjective harms; define targeted vs open-ended objectives; use domain experts, AI experts and target end users with diversity; track acceptable response rate, refusal rate and turns-to-unsafe; annotators may be red teamers, independent third parties or LLM judges with human sampling; automated red teaming (e.g. PAIR, Crescendo-style) is an emerging complement.

Accountability principle: a System must have mechanisms for responsibility and accountability; these may include internal governance and control frameworks or regular external auditing (examples only).
All actors are to conduct appropriate risk analyses and take countermeasures against identified risks.
AI operators should define a suitable fallback plan and test it, including thresholds for acceptable results.
Fully test the product before deployment, have robust assurance and regular checks of the live tool, and provide ways for users to report issues that prompt human review.

clause_or_page: s4.6.10, p.11 of 17 (Minimum acceptable requirements for AI tools)
requirement_paraphrase: AI software and major upgraded versions must comply with all required certification from recognised bodies (text truncated in tool output after 'recognised international or local agencies').

Set of voluntary guidelines for pre-deployment testing of LLM apps for baseline safety and reliability across five risks: hallucination/inaccuracy, bias in decision making, undesirable content, data leakage, and vulnerability to adversarial prompts.
Recommends AI-specific penetration testing of AI system components before deployment and periodically afterwards, including testing outputs and system behaviour.

Services with public opinion attributes or social mobilisation capacity must complete a security assessment under national rules and complete algorithm filing under the algorithm recommendation provisions.

For Annex III points 2 to 8 (critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice/democracy) providers follow the internal-control procedure of Annex VI with no notified body.

Suggested actions include testing and evaluating systems in non-optimised conditions, measuring systems before deployment in conditions similar to expected scenarios, measuring validity (false positive/negative rates) and efficiency against ground truth in deployment context, and documenting differences between measurement setting and deployment environment.
Developers and operators could consider formal procedures such as Discrimination Impact Assessments to help ensure fair decisions.
AI systems informing critical decisions should be subject to appropriate external audit; publishing the results should be considered.
Implement post-deployment monitoring plans, including capturing input from users and AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery and change management.

clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.5.2, printed p.15; Implementation Guidance 3.5.2 (Defending Against AI/ML Attacks), printed p.38
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must deploy comprehensive defences for AI/ML systems including continuous monitoring and regular testing. Guidance: regular security testing, including penetration testing and red-teaming exercises, should be run on AI/ML systems to find weaknesses; defensive techniques (e.g. adversarial training) should be built in during development and deployment.

Technical report on properties, risks, methods and processes for AI in safety functions, non-AI safety functions protecting AI-controlled equipment, and AI used to develop safety functions; published Jan 2024, 73 pages.

AI used in healthcare activities should have graceful-degradation mechanisms with automatic alerts; should be subject to audits and examination by the technology provider; and healthcare end-users must conduct regular audits of AI functionality and report to DoH as needed.
Recommends approval processes for high-impact AI before production deployment, ensuring cybersecurity risks are assessed and addressed.
Develop guardrails to detect and prevent malicious input, unauthorised actions and sensitive information disclosure, and ensure they are tested before production use and after material changes.

Safety mitigations must be robust under adversarial pressure, and signatories carry out post-market monitoring (feedback channels, incident forms, bug bounties and similar) to inform whether the risk stays acceptable.

clause_or_page: s.2.3.2 'Before deploying, test agents', case study box 'Google x Singapore Government: Testing computer use agents', p.40 (v1.5)
requirement_paraphrase: Case study (descriptive): Google, CSA, GovTech and IMDA ran a sandbox testing computer-use agents for three potential public-sector uses (automated QA of government digital services, automated AI safety testing of third-party chatbots, social assistance applications). Lessons: use realistic test data and environments; log and evaluate the agent's reasoning at each step; identify use-case-specific attack vectors such as indirect prompt injection; keep humans in the loop during testing. Findings: the agent included extraneous personal details in a significant number of cases and in some instances navigated to arbitrary URLs when instructed by injected content.

Lists a spectrum of assurance mechanisms - risk assessment, impact assessment, bias audit, compliance audit, conformity assessment (often including performance testing), formal verification - to be used in combination across the AI lifecycle, proportionate to risk.

clause_or_page: Principle 2, Deploy and Monitor item 3, p. 17
requirement_paraphrase: The AI system should be tested to ensure the combination of available data does not reveal sensitive data or break anonymity.
When a vulnerability is detected, disable or restrict vulnerable AI features until remediation is validated.

Suggested actions include red-team exercises under adversarial or stress conditions, documenting red-team results, and using separate testing teams (set up under GOVERN) so that decisions about AI systems are independent; assess independence and stature of TEVV actors.

Signatories obtain assurance that security mitigations meet the Security Goal through independent external security reviews where internal expertise is inadequate, frequent red-teaming of network and physical access management, competitive bug bounties for public-facing endpoints, periodic personnel integrity testing, third-party security reporting channels, endpoint/intrusion detection tools and a security incident response team.

clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.1.2, printed p.11; Implementation Guidance 3.1.2 (Cyber Risk Management for AI/ML), printed p.19
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must identify, assess and mitigate AI-specific cyber security risks systematically and continuously. Guidance: cyber risk assessments should be run at regular intervals and at key lifecycle stages such as model design, data collection, training and deployment, including risks of cloud AI services that use client data.

clause_or_page: Ch. 10.3 (AI Ethics Policy) and 10.2 (Initiative Approval), printed p. 87
requirement_paraphrase: States that every AI initiative under DDA must demonstrate alignment with DDA's ethical principles and undergo rigorous validation for ethical compliance across its lifecycle, and passes a standard approval workflow including technical feasibility, business case, risk evaluation and resource sign-off.

clause_or_page: AI Safety Institute approach to evaluations (published 2024-02-09), sections 'AISI's approach to evaluations'
requirement_paraphrase: AISI conducts pre-deployment and post-deployment evaluations of advanced AI systems using automated capability assessments, expert red-teaming, human uplift studies and AI agent evaluations, focusing on misuse (chemical/biological, cyber), societal impacts, autonomous systems and safeguards.
AI systems rated high risk must undergo conformity assessments both before and after deployment, coordinated with DoH's Data and Digital Governance Office.

Avoid extrapolating performance from narrow or anecdotal assessments; review and verify sources and citations in outputs during pre-deployment measurement and monitoring; regularly review safety/security guardrails, including reasons the system was initially judged safe to deploy.

clause_or_page: Trusted Development and Deployment dimension, 'Evaluation', p.14 (government-transparency sentence in 'Disclosure', p.14)
requirement_paraphrase: Benchmarking and red teaming are the two main evaluation approaches today but fall far short of a robust assessment (front-end focus, missing tools incl. dangerous-capability tests, poor comparability); the framework calls for a more comprehensive, systematic safety evaluation approach that could include a baseline set of required safety tests developed in consultation with policymakers; the adjacent Disclosure text says greater transparency to government will be needed for potentially high-risk models.
Operators should consider working with their vendors (AI developers) to continually monitor system performance.
Part 3 will give a methodology for using statistical methods to evaluate neural network robustness; at stage 50.00 (FDIS) with an August 2026 stage date, not shown as published on the page read.

Check robustness (varied, perturbed, adversarial phrasing) and consistency (repeat runs); test breadth and depth scaled to stakes, repeating tests and evaluating average, minimum and maximum scores; if resources are limited, either use a subset instead of full benchmarks, or run the full set once and repeat a targeted subset (e.g. borderline prompts).

Each ministry's Chief AI Officer (CAIO), with planners, shall conduct use-case risk assessments and determine the risk level (including whether likely high-risk), referring to the High-Risk AI Project Finder (Appendix 1); likely high-risk cases are reported to the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board; the CAIO makes the final determination.
Providers must implement entity responsibility for algorithm security, including algorithm mechanism review and technology ethics review.

Signatory organisations commit to assess risks of frontier models across the lifecycle, including before deployment, considering results from internal and external evaluations such as independent third-party evaluators and home governments.
AI systems with very high residual risk after controls must be prohibited from deployment.
Operators should subject AI systems informing significant decisions to quality checks at least as stringent as those applied to a human decision maker.

Data scientists are to test AI systems to assess risks, confirm intended performance and compliance with healthcare and safety regulations, assess robustness, fairness and accuracy, and document metrics and logs; data users identify groups at risk of disparate outcomes and report use of relevant attributes.

Systemic-risk GPAI providers must assess and mitigate systemic risks at Union level, track and report serious incidents to the AI Office, and ensure adequate cybersecurity for the model and its physical infrastructure.

Use use-case-appropriate benchmarks to quantify bias, stereotyping and hateful content, documenting benchmark assumptions and possible train/test contamination; conduct fairness assessments across demographic groups using field testing with sub-groups, red-teaming with counterfactual prompts, and general fairness metrics where outcomes are categorical or numeric.
AI developers should consider whether their systems can be expected to perform well on previously unseen data, especially for people under-represented in training data.

clause_or_page: s3.8.2.2 body text, p.42 (heading concerns an oversight mechanism for data)
requirement_paraphrase: Privacy impact assessments should be conducted and also cover societal and ethical considerations.

clause_or_page: s.2.3.3 'When deploying, continuously monitor and test', case study 'GovTech: Phased rollouts of coding assistants', pp.42-43
requirement_paraphrase: Case study: GovTech (statutory board) rolled out agentic coding assistants (Windsurf, GitHub Copilot Agent Mode from Oct 2025; Claude Code from Apr 2026) after extensive tests on failure and threat vectors such as agent manipulation, hallucination and MCP server compromise and after implementing controls; phase 1 limited to GovTech employees, no MCP access and low-risk systems; before phase 2 (other agencies, then vendors) red teaming was conducted to validate guardrails, with central logging and a sandboxed MCP governance path.

For high-risk systems in Annex I Section A products, the provider follows the sectoral conformity assessment procedure, Section 2 requirements form part of it, QMS assessment is added, and notified bodies under sectoral law must apply for AI Act designation by 28 January 2028.
